claim: Alphabet's total Traffic Acquisition Costs (TAC) rose from $54,900 million in FY2024 to $59,926 million in FY2025, a $5.0 billion increase.
stance_target: magnitude of Google's search/network distribution payments
scope_conditions: Alphabet consolidated, FY2024 vs FY2025 (years ended Dec 31)
quoted_support: TAC | 54,900 | 59,926 ... Cost of revenues increased $16.2 billion from 2024 to 2025 due to an increase in other cost of revenues and TAC of $11.2 billion and $5.0 billion, respectively.

claim: The increase in Alphabet's TAC from 2024 to 2025 was largely driven by higher TAC paid to distribution partners (e.g., Apple, browser/OEM/carrier partners), not to Google Network Members.
stance_target: distribution-partner (including Apple) TAC is the growth driver, not ad-network TAC
quoted_support: The increase in TAC from 2024 to 2025 was largely due to an increase in TAC paid to distribution partners, primarily driven by growth in revenues subject to TAC.

claim: Alphabet's overall TAC rate (TAC as % of advertising revenue) fell from 20.7% to 20.3% from 2024 to 2025, attributed to a revenue mix shift toward Google Search & other properties, not to per-partner rate compression.
quoted_support: The TAC rate decreased from 20.7% to 20.3% from 2024 to 2025, primarily due to a revenue mix shift from Google Network properties to Google Search & other properties. The TAC rates on Google Search & other and Google Network revenues were substantially consistent from 2024 to 2025.

claim: Alphabet's FY2025 10-K does not disclose a specific dollar figure for TAC paid to distribution partners separately from TAC paid to Google Network Members; only qualitative attribution of the y/y change is given.
stance_target: disclosure granularity of Apple-specific TAC magnitude
quoted_support: amounts paid to our distribution partners who make available our search access points and other ad-supported services... and amounts paid to Google Network partners primarily for ads displayed on their properties.

claim: In the DOJ/states v. Google search case (D.D.C., filed Oct 2020), the district court ruled against Google in August 2024, entered a final remedies judgment in December 2025 restricting distribution practices and requiring data-sharing/syndication obligations, Google appealed and moved to stay implementation in January 2026, and DOJ/state AGs cross-appealed in February 2026.
stance_target: appellate posture and timeline of the US v. Google search remedies case
scope_conditions: D.D.C. case 1:20-cv-03010 (case number not stated verbatim in 10-K text but matches known docket); FY2025 10-K legal proceedings disclosure
quoted_support: A final judgment was entered in December 2025, which, among other things, imposes restrictions on how Google distributes its services and requires Google to share certain search data with and offer syndication services to certain competitors. In January 2026, we appealed the final judgment and moved to pause implementation of certain remedies. In February 2026, the DOJ and state Attorneys General also appealed.
entities: US District Court for the District of Columbia

claim: A separate DOJ/states ad-tech antitrust case (E.D. Va.) found Google's publisher tools unfairly excluded rivals in April 2025; a remedies trial occurred September-November 2025 with the DOJ proposing structural remedies, and Google was still awaiting the remedies judgment as of the FY2025 10-K filing date (Feb 2026), planning to appeal both the liability finding and any adverse remedies.
stance_target: status of the separate ad-tech antitrust case, distinct from the search-distribution case
scope_conditions: US District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, DOJ v. Google ad-tech case
quoted_support: A separate proceeding to determine remedies, the range of which vary widely, took place in September 2025, with the parties presenting differing remedy proposals. The DOJ's remedy proposal includes structural remedies that could have a material adverse effect on our business. Closing arguments were held in November 2025, and we are awaiting a final judgment.
entities: US District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia

claim: Alphabet's Sales and Marketing expenses rose only $885 million (2024 to 2025) and G&A rose $7.3 billion, largely due to a $3.5 billion EC ad-tech fine accrued Q3 2025 and a $1.4 billion legal accrual in Q2 2025 -- both unrelated to the TAC/search-distribution line but material to overall antitrust-cost exposure.
stance_target: scale of Alphabet's aggregate antitrust-related cost exposure beyond TAC
quoted_support: General and administrative expenses increased $7.3 billion from 2024 to 2025, primarily driven by an increase in expenses related to legal and other matters of $6.2 billion, largely the result of the $3.5 billion EC fine accrued in the third quarter of 2025 and a $1.4 billion legal accrual made in the second quarter of 2025.
